title: Bug: [sflow] PTF script assumes that port index map starts at zero
author: anders-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

In the sflow/test_sflow.py PTF script, the port map is assumed to start at zero, which is not guaranteed to always be the case. We are already pulling the src_port in this script, so we can just use that since we know it. This way we don't have to rely on a specific port mapping:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/4082f1c4ed254713508e2908dc3a84c74a81b6af/ansible/roles/test/files/ptftests/py3/sflow_test.py#L260

### Steps to Reproduce

On a testbed where the PTF index map does not start at zero, run the test and you will see something like the following:
```
ATTENTION: SOME TESTS DID NOT PASS!!!

The following tests errored:
SflowTest

******************************************stderr =
sflow_test.SflowTest ... ERROR

======================================================================
ERROR: sflow_test.SflowTest
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/ptftests/py3/sflow_test.py", line 306, in runTest
    self.sendTraffic()
  File "/root/ptftests/py3/sflow_test.py", line 270, in sendTraffic
    src_mac = self.dataplane.get_mac(0, 0)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/env-python3/lib/python3.11/site-packages/ptf/dataplane.py", line 1003, in get_mac
    return self.ports[(device_number, port_number)].mac()
           ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: (0, 0)
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Expected: The test should work on testbeds with ptf index maps that do not start at zero (why else would we even have the ptf index map at all?)

Actual: The test fails with the error shown above.

Summary:
In the sflow PTF script, the port map is assumed to start at zero, which is not always the case. The code calls 'self.dataplane.get_mac(0,0)' in order to get a source port MAC. A few lines later, the code gets the actual port to send the traffic, so we can use that source port MAC instead (which is more correct anyway).

Closes #21185

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Tests should not make assumptions about the underlying testbed network structure without a good reason. This change makes test_sflow.py more general.

#### How did you do it?

Instead of defaulting to port index zero and passing the same source port for every packet, we can use the source port for each given interface (since we're already looking them up) and pass that instead.

#### How did you verify/test it?

The test fails when run on a testbed with a PTF port index map that doesn't start at zero.

With these changes, the test passes on those testbeds.
